data.description: Instance data

200.description: Request processed. Check `ok`: a business validation failure also returns HTTP 200, with ok=false and the reason in `error`.

ok.description: True if the instance was saved. Business validation failures are reported as HTTP 200 with ok=false and a message in `error` - always check this flag.

newId.description: Id of the saved Recibo (the new id when creating, the same id when updating). This is the field that carries the identifier - there is no `id` field in this response.

error.description: Error message when ok=false. Null on success.

parameter.description: The full saved instance, serialized as a JSON **string** (not a nested object) - same content as GET /COBRO/{id} with includeChildren=true. Parse it to read it.

400.description: Bad request - invalid data, missing required fields, or a field the caller is not allowed to write (`errors` names which one, keyed by its path in the payload)

errors.description: Per-field errors (RFC 7807 ValidationProblemDetails), keyed by the field's path in the request payload. The key is the physical attribute name for a header field (`ORDV_CLIE_ID`), or the full path including the row index for a field inside a nested child collection (`Cobros[0].COBR_R_D_TARJETA`). `title` stays generic, so this is where the offending field is named.

schema.description:
Error payload. Read whichever of these is present: endpoint validations return `error`, state-change/delete results return `message`, and domain exceptions are mapped to RFC 7807 ProblemDetails (`title` / `status`).

When the payload includes a field the caller is not allowed to write, `errors` names which one - do not parse `title` for it, it is deliberately generic.

schema.description:
A Recibo instance.

Only Recibo's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /COBRO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /COBRO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.description:

The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Recibo's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /COBRO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /COBRO/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Recibo instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /CONTROL_FACTURAS_ONL/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Control Facturas Online instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

200.description: Request processed. Check `ok`: a business validation failure also returns HTTP 200, with ok=false and the reason in `error`.

ok.description: True if the instance was saved. Business validation failures are reported as HTTP 200 with ok=false and a message in `error` - always check this flag.

newId.description: Id of the saved Factura (the new id when creating, the same id when updating). This is the field that carries the identifier - there is no `id` field in this response.

error.description: Error message when ok=false. Null on success.

parameter.description: The full saved instance, serialized as a JSON **string** (not a nested object) - same content as GET /FACTURA/{id} with includeChildren=true. Parse it to read it.

400.description: Bad request - invalid data, missing required fields, or a field the caller is not allowed to write (`errors` names which one, keyed by its path in the payload)

errors.description: Per-field errors (RFC 7807 ValidationProblemDetails), keyed by the field's path in the request payload. The key is the physical attribute name for a header field (`ORDV_CLIE_ID`), or the full path including the row index for a field inside a nested child collection (`Cobros[0].COBR_R_D_TARJETA`). `title` stays generic, so this is where the offending field is named.

schema.description:

When the payload includes a field the caller is not allowed to write, `errors` names which one - do not parse `title` for it, it is deliberately generic.

schema.description:
A Factura instance.

Only Factura's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /FACTURA/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /FACTURA/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Fast search endpoint. Returns a capped, non-paginated set of Factura records; prefer /query for controlled, production-grade listings.
get.description:
Performs a lightweight search over Factura instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Factura's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /FACTURA/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /FACTURA/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

200.description: Matching instances, as a flat array (not wrapped in an object). Child entities are not included.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /FACTURA/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Factura instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /LIQ_DE_COMISIONES/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Liq. de comisiones instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

data.description: Instance data

200.description: Request processed. Check `ok`: a business validation failure also returns HTTP 200, with ok=false and the reason in `error`.

ok.description: True if the instance was saved. Business validation failures are reported as HTTP 200 with ok=false and a message in `error` - always check this flag.

newId.description: Id of the saved Pedido (the new id when creating, the same id when updating). This is the field that carries the identifier - there is no `id` field in this response.

error.description: Error message when ok=false. Null on success.

parameter.description: The full saved instance, serialized as a JSON **string** (not a nested object) - same content as GET /PEDIDO/{id} with includeChildren=true. Parse it to read it.

400.description: Bad request - invalid data, missing required fields, or a field the caller is not allowed to write (`errors` names which one, keyed by its path in the payload)

errors.description: Per-field errors (RFC 7807 ValidationProblemDetails), keyed by the field's path in the request payload. The key is the physical attribute name for a header field (`ORDV_CLIE_ID`), or the full path including the row index for a field inside a nested child collection (`Cobros[0].COBR_R_D_TARJETA`). `title` stays generic, so this is where the offending field is named.

schema.description:
Error payload. Read whichever of these is present: endpoint validations return `error`, state-change/delete results return `message`, and domain exceptions are mapped to RFC 7807 ProblemDetails (`title` / `status`).

When the payload includes a field the caller is not allowed to write, `errors` names which one - do not parse `title` for it, it is deliberately generic.

attsFkTexts.title: Foreign key texts
attsFkTexts.description: Descriptive text of every foreign key / user / profile / fixed-value attribute that has a value, keyed by physical name (included when includeFkTexts=true). Example: `"TIDD_ID_TIDD": "CUIT"`. Attributes without a value are omitted, not returned as empty.

schema.description:
A Pedido instance.

Only Pedido's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /PEDIDO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /PEDIDO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Fast search endpoint. Returns a capped, non-paginated set of Pedido records; prefer /query for controlled, production-grade listings.
get.description:
Performs a lightweight search over Pedido instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Pedido's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /PEDIDO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /PEDIDO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

200.description: Matching instances, as a flat array (not wrapped in an object). Child entities are not included.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /PEDIDO/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Pedido instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Carga resumida de Recibos V2 instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /CHEQUE/query`.

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Cheque Recibido instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Cobro de Pedido instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /COBRO_ELECTRONICO/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Cobro electrónico instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Cobro MP instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Depósito bancario instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Cobro en Efectivo instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Novedad Fact. Detalle instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /NOVEDAD_FACTURA/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Novedad Factura instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Novedad NC instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator
