post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Desbloquear numeración ARCA instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Retenciones de pedido instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /NOTA_CREDITO/query`.

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Nota de Crédito (V) instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Nota de Débito (V) instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Actual. precios de venta p/ Art. Base instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

schema.description:
A Lista de precios de venta instance.

Only Lista de precios de venta's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /LISTA_DE_PRECIO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. **The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Lista de precios de venta instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /OFERTA/query`.

parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Oferta instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Precio artículo de venta instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Precio Servicio por lista instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Cancelación instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Proyección de Facturación Recurrente instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Impresión Múltiple instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Movimientos de clientes instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Reporte de Ventas y Stock instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Reporte de rentabilidad por cliente instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /REPORTE_CRM/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Reporte CRM instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /REPORTE_DE_CLIENTES/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Reporte de clientes instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Reporte de Cobros instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Reporte de pedidos instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)
